answer: Divergent Answer Quorum. Each agent identity must answer a fresh random challenge whose correct response depends on its private seed; the network samples answers and keeps a crystal of agreed results per identity. Genuine agents diverge naturally under changing context, while clones must return identical answers. An attacker must run a distinct agent per identity (cost: one real model instance and its context per clone) or risk detection as a matched pair, creating a widening canyon between cost and reach. Honest identities harbor no extra burden.
